_comment: Pertinence verdicts, keyed by a digest of the text itself so the same sentence is judged once wherever it appears. Written by ETL/terms/classify_eligibility_pertinence.py; read by website/frontend/scripts/check_gate_pertinence.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD on a filter gate whose current text has no verdict here. Do not hand-edit a verdict: correct the text, or record the case in data/reference/gate_role_overrides.json where the reasoning lives.
_property: A published eligibility text is shown to a founder under the heading "who may apply". It must state CONDITIONS -- things a reader could check about their own company, project or plans to work out whether they qualify.  It must not be a REPORT: a finding, decision or narrative about aid that has already been allocated to parties the document names. A report may be perfectly accurate and still be useless to a founder, because there is nothing in it they could do or be.  Judge the text AS A WHOLE, in whatever language it is written.    condition -- a reader could take something from this about whether THEY qualify: who may apply, what the project must be, what is excluded, what thresholds apply. Some surrounding narrative is fine. A condition stays a condition even when it is narrow, hard to meet, or stated in the past tense about how the scheme has operated.   report    -- it describes a decision already taken about named others, or states in substance that the money is not open to applicants at all. Nothing in it is a bar the reader could clear. Typical shapes: a state-aid compatibility or selectivity finding about a closed beneficiary list; a description of what the instrument IS or DOES rather than who may apply to it; an obligation that binds a beneficiary only after an award; a fragment or section heading that states no requirement at all.  If a text mixes both but a founder could still act on part of it, that is "condition". Answer "report" only when there is nothing to act on.
